q: Which statement about a constructor in C++ is correct?
options: It has the same name as its class and no return type
It must return an int value
exp: A constructor carries the class name and has no return type (not even void); it cannot be static or virtual.

q: In C++, when a class is derived using private inheritance, the public members of the base class become ____ members of the derived class.
exp: Private inheritance makes all accessible base members (public and protected) private in the derived class.

q: Which of the following is an example of compile-time (static) polymorphism?
options: Overriding a method of an abstract class
exp: Overloaded calls are resolved by the compiler from the argument list; overriding is resolved at run time.

q: Encapsulation in OOP means:
options: Deriving a new class from an existing class
Using one name for many different forms
Showing only the essential features to the user
Binding data and the functions that operate on it into one unit and restricting direct access to the data
exp: Encapsulation wraps data and methods together in a class and controls access to the data using access specifiers.
The thrown value is an int, so the catch(int) handler matches before the catch-all handler: it prints int 10.

q: The Java compiler (javac) translates source code into:
options: Native machine code of the host CPU
Object code specific to the operating system
exp: javac produces platform-independent bytecode (.class files), which the JVM interprets or JIT-compiles.

q: In C++, which file-opening mode flag makes an ofstream add output at the end of an existing file without erasing its old content?
exp: By default an ofstream truncates (erases) an existing file. ios::app positions every write at the end, so old content is kept; ios::trunc erases, ios::in is for reading, ios::binary only selects binary mode.

q: A static member function in C++ can directly access:
options: Only static data members and other static member functions
exp: A static function belongs to the class, has no this pointer, and so can directly use only static members.

q: Which keyword is used in Java to inherit a class from another class?
exp: A class inherits another class using extends; implements is used for interfaces.
f is virtual, so the call through the base pointer is bound at run time to B::f.

q: Which of the following is true for an abstract class in Java?
options: It can contain both abstract and concrete methods but cannot be instantiated
It cannot contain any concrete method
It can be instantiated using new
exp: An abstract class may mix abstract and implemented methods, but objects cannot be created from it directly.

q: Which is the correct way to start a function template declaration in C++?
exp: Function templates begin with template <class T> (or template <typename T>) before the function.
Strings are immutable; concat returns a new String that is discarded, so s remains Hi.

q: Which class of the java.io package is designed to read a text file as a stream of characters?
exp: FileReader reads characters; FileInputStream reads raw bytes, FileWriter writes characters and PrintStream is an output stream.

q: Which statement about C++ destructors is correct?
options: A class can have several overloaded destructors
A destructor can take one int parameter
A destructor has no parameters and cannot be overloaded
A destructor must always be called explicitly
exp: A destructor is written ~ClassName(), takes no arguments and has no return type, so only one exists per class.

q: For class Derived : public Base, when an object of Derived is created, the constructors run in the order:
options: Order is decided at run time
exp: Base sub-objects are constructed first, then the derived part.

q: Which change alone does NOT allow two Java methods in the same class to be overloaded?
options: Changing the type of a parameter
Changing the order of parameters of different types
exp: Overloading requires different parameter lists; a different return type alone causes a compile-time error.

q: In Java, variables declared inside an interface are implicitly:
exp: Interface fields are constants: public, static and final.
The extraction operator >> reads whitespace-separated ints: a = 10, b = 20, so a + b = 30. The third value 30 is never read.

q: Which method of the Thread class is used to begin execution of a new thread in Java?
exp: start() creates a new call stack and invokes run() in it.
r is a reference (alias) of x, so r++ increments x to 6.

q: In a non-static member function of a C++ class, the this pointer points to:
options: The object on which the function was invoked
The base class of the current class
The first member of the class
exp: this holds the address of the invoking (current) object.

q: Which of the following is NOT a recognised type of inheritance in OOP?
exp: Single, multiple, multilevel, hierarchical and hybrid are standard types; circular inheritance is illegal.

q: Which is the correct declaration of a pure virtual function in C++?
exp: A pure virtual function is declared with = 0 after the declarator.

q: A member of a Java class declared protected is accessible:
options: Within its package and by subclasses in other packages
exp: protected gives package access plus access through inheritance in other packages.

q: In Java, the finally block:
options: Executes only when an exception is thrown
Executes whether or not an exception occurs
Executes only when no exception occurs
Cannot be used without a catch block
exp: finally is meant for clean-up and runs in both normal and exceptional flow (and may follow try alone).
Control jumps to case 2 and prints B; there is no break, so it falls through to case 3 and prints C, then break leaves the switch. Output: BC.

q: In a UML class diagram, a line ending in a hollow (unfilled) diamond represents:
exp: Hollow diamond is aggregation (weak has-a); a filled diamond is composition.

q: In C++, the copy constructor is invoked when:
options: An object is passed by reference to a function
An object is passed by value to a function
A pointer to an object is declared
exp: Passing by value creates a copy of the argument, calling the copy constructor.

q: In Java, the super keyword is used to refer to:
exp: super refers to the immediate superclass's members and constructors.

q: Which statement is correct about method overriding in Java?
options: The overriding method must have a different parameter list
The overriding method may be private when the original is public
The overriding method cannot have a more restrictive access modifier
The call is resolved at compile time
exp: Overriding must keep the same signature and cannot reduce visibility; dispatch is at run time.

q: Why can a Java class achieve a form of multiple inheritance through interfaces?
options: A class can implement more than one interface
A class can extend two interfaces
exp: A class may implement any number of interfaces, thereby inheriting several types.

q: Which of the following is a checked exception in Java?
exp: IOException is checked and must be caught or declared; the others are RuntimeExceptions.
